reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that prediction markets exhibit payoff identities—specifically, ΣY_i ≡ 1 for YES outcomes and ΣN_k ≡ (|Q|-1) for NO outcomes—which define a geometric constraint on valid market states. When these identities are violated, they indicate either theoretical bounds or executable arbitrage opportunities. Settlement edges Δ^settle_Y and Δ^settle_N quantify deviation from payoff identity in terms of normalized prices. Converter edges Δ^{N→Y}_S allow for arbitrage via NO→YES conversion, provided the reverse path (YES→NO) lacks protocol support. These primitives form a dual structure: one for settlement-based arbitrage and another for converter-based arbitrage. Violation episodes arise when these edges remain positive over time, indicating persistent mispricing. The failure mode occurs when the reverse path is unsupported, leading to asymmetric exploitation. This dualism enables GSE to monitor both directions of arbitrage while GSI validates the underlying payoff constraints.
